title: Strawberry-rhubarb pie
summary: Mostly rhubarb with a smaller share of strawberries, lightly set with xanthan gum under an almond-pastry lattice.
steps: Pulse the almond flour, psyllium, xanthan gum, erythritol and salt in a food processor. Add the butter and egg and pulse until the dough comes together. Divide into two-thirds and one-third, flatten each into a disc and chill 30 minutes.

Roll the larger piece between two sheets of parchment to a 28 cm (11 in) round and flip it into a 23 cm (9 in) pie plate. Patch any cracks with your fingers. Roll the smaller piece to a rectangle and cut 2 cm (3/4 in) strips.

Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Toss the rhubarb and strawberries with the lemon juice and vanilla. Whisk the erythritol and xanthan gum together and sprinkle over the fruit, tossing so no clumps remain.
Pile the fruit into the crust. Lay the strips over it in a lattice, pressing the ends onto the rim, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake 15 minutes, then lower to 175 °C (350 °F) and bake 30–35 minutes more, until the filling bubbles in the centre. Cover the edge with foil if it darkens.
Cool at least 3 hours so the juices set before slicing.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter makes a slightly softer pastry; keep the lattice strips well chilled so they hold their shape.
tips: Whisking the xanthan gum into the sweetener first is the only way to keep it from forming slimy lumps.
Rhubarb is the low-carb backbone here; adding more strawberries raises the carbs quickly.

origin.history: Rhubarb was grown for centuries as a medicinal root before its stalks became a common food in Britain and North America in the 1800s. Americans baked it so often that it was nicknamed 'pie plant'. Strawberries ripen in the same late-spring weeks, and the two became a classic pairing of American home baking in the 1900s.
